craft_notes: Sthāyin: naming-climax (Śaivī — speech itself). Sanskrit: śaktyavasthāpraviṣṭasya...śivarūpī syāt śaivī mukham iha ucyate → L4 ends on named-mouth. Rows: row 1 (undivided contemplation). Rupture: colon after formed — then, then the name. Close: Śaivī (the name lands last-but-mouth: 'mouth is called Śaivī' — end-weight on the coined name). Rejected: 'Śaiva' — killed: feminine Śaivī is the coined mouth-name; dropping 'mouth' — killed: mukham is the point (speech as door).

lines: Of one entered the power-state, contemplation
undivided: then he Śiva-formed — the mouth is called Śaivī.
l4.sanskrit_cite: śaktyavasthāpraviṣṭasya nirvibhāgena bhāvanā | tadāsau śivarūpī syāt śaivī mukham ihocyate

reads_against.argmap: What happens on entering power-state? → Undivided contemplation makes him Śiva-formed — that mouth is called Śaivī.
c1_essence: Entered power-state, undivided contemplation: Śiva-formed, Śaivī named.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder of the unspeakable)
